clue.text: Comfort for Bill in exclusive surroundings

indicators.note: exclusive supplies the outer word, forming surroundings round the bill

parts.note: sole means exclusive, as in sole rights
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Someone finds consolation in paying a bill somewhere select and private.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surroundings' puts AC (account, a bill) inside SOLE (exclusive).
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is consolation given in distress, so it is comfort.

clue.text: One showing good humour when left in vessel with crew

indicators.note: in places the word for left inside the vessel's letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a vessel
port is the left side of a ship
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A cheerful type is abandoned aboard ship with the sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts PORT inside SS, then MAN follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportsman is someone who takes defeat or teasing gracefully, a good loser.

clue.text: A permissive occupation?

parts.note: permissive read as allowing, and occupation as tenancy of a house rented out

explanation.surface: A job for someone lax.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting is allowing, and also renting out property for others to occupy.

clue.text: Empty case with one way drawer

indicators.note: with indicates the case holding the zero for nothing inside it

parts.note: a carton is a cardboard case
O, zero, stands for nothing, empty
I is the Roman numeral one
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A hollow box comes with a single-direction drawer, like furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' puts O (empty) inside CARTON, then I and ST follow. 'drawer' suggests a sliding box but is one who draws.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoonist is an artist who draws comic pictures.

clue.text: Appropriate homily given to sailors

parts.note: ABs are able seamen, so sailors in the plural
a tract is a short moralising pamphlet, a homily

explanation.surface: A suitable sermon is handed out to the crew of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to take for oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract something is to remove or steal it, which is to appropriate it.

clue.text: A great advantage on moors in rural America

parts.note: a boon is a blessing, a great advantage
to moor a ship is to berth or dock it

explanation.surface: Wild moorland is a real benefit in the American countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moors' looks like heathland but is the verb. BOONDOCKS is American slang for remote backwoods.
explanation.definitionFit: The boondocks are remote rural back-country areas in the United States.

clue.text: Tight race to secure gold

indicators.note: secure means hold fast, so the race encloses the gold

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorbike race on the Isle of Man
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A closely fought contest with the gold medal at stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' puts AU inside TT.
explanation.definitionFit: Taut means stretched tight, as a rope.

clue.text: A superior assistant

parts.note: better means superior

explanation.surface: A top-notch helper.
explanation.definitionFit: An abetter helps someone, especially in wrongdoing, so is an accomplice or helper.

clue.text: Giant bird starts to assemble nest

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: starts to means take the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A huge bird begins to build its home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' gives A and N from assemble and nest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were giant gods of Greek myth; a titan is any colossus.

clue.text: Made progress by crawling, perhaps

parts.note: the crawl here is the swimming stroke, not moving on hands and knees

explanation.surface: Advanced by creeping along.
explanation.definitionFit: Front crawl is a swimming stroke, so moving through water using it means one swims.

clue.text: Produced abroad to start with, then over-expanded

indicators.note: says the word for abroad comes first, before the word for produced

parts.note: out can mean abroad, away from home
grew as in grew crops, produced them

explanation.surface: Something cultivated overseas at first then got too big.
explanation.definitionFit: To outgrow is to become too large for something, expanding beyond its limits.

clue.text: Ordered no let up, having plenty of money

indicators.note: ordered means arranged afresh, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone rich insists there be no easing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' rearranges NO LET UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulent describes wealth and lavish riches.

clue.text: Perfectly turned-out model at air crash

indicators.note: a crash wrecks things, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A smartly dressed fashion model is caught up in a plane accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' rearranges MODEL AT AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes made by a tailor fit exactly, so a tailor-made look is perfectly turned out.

clue.text: Surprise return of cuckoo

indicators.note: return means the word for cuckoo is read backwards

parts.note: cuckoo and nuts both mean crazy

explanation.surface: The bird coming back in spring is unexpected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns NUTS (crazy) round.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to astonish or amaze, a strong surprise.

clue.text: Uncertain batting, that's for sure

parts.note: a cricketer batting is in
definite means sure, beyond doubt

explanation.surface: A batsman is unsure, though insists he is certain.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side batting is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Indefinite means unclear or not fixed, so doubtful.

clue.text: A colourful battle

explanation.surface: A battle full of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The purplish-red dye was named after a battle of 1859 in northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a vivid purplish-red hue, and also the Italian town where French and Sardinian forces beat Austria.

clue.text: As smooth as this party wearing a flower

indicators.note: the party is worn inside, so its letters sit within the others

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower
Lab is short for the Labour Party

explanation.surface: A party guest with a flower in the lapel is extremely suave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' places LAB inside A + ASTER. Alabaster is the standard of smoothness and whiteness.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a fine translucent stone proverbial for its silky surface.

clue.text: Rascal is behind, unable to spell

indicators.note: the rascal stands behind, after the word for unable

parts.note: can't means unable
rip is an old word for a scamp or rascal

explanation.surface: A naughty child lags behind because he cannot spell.
explanation.walkthrough: CANTRIP is a Scots word for a witch's spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantrip is a magic charm or trick, a witch's incantation.

clue.text: Early Christmas present adorning tree

parts.note: the carol gives a bird in a pear tree on the first of the twelve days

explanation.surface: An early gift decorating the festive fir.
explanation.walkthrough: The carol The Twelve Days of Christmas begins with a bird in a pear tree.
explanation.definitionFit: In the carol a game bird sitting in a fruit tree is the first-day gift.

clue.text: Bloomer by Mensa — that's surprising!

indicators.note: surprising suggests letters turned in an unexpected way, rearranged

parts.note: i.e. is short for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A howler made by the high-IQ society would indeed be a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprising' rearranges MENSA plus IE (that is). 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesia is a garden flower, so a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Grisly vehicle and what may have drawn it around

indicators.note: around puts the horse round the vehicle

parts.note: a horse-drawn cab was pulled by a mare
a cab is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A gruesome hearse with its horse in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts CAB inside MARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means gruesome and dwelling on death.

clue.text: Hasten to repair component of loudspeaker

indicators.note: component of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Hurry to fix a part of the sound system.
explanation.walkthrough: Stentor was the Greek herald in the Iliad with a voice as loud as fifty men.
explanation.definitionFit: A stentor is a person with a very powerful voice, a speaker who is loud.

clue.text: Digging possibly reveals money box with silver quarter

parts.note: a till holds a shop's cash
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
E, east, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: An excavation turns up a cash box with silverware.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is working the soil, as by digging or ploughing.

clue.text: Principal leader removed from demonstration

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which is taken off the word for a demonstration

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration

explanation.surface: The chief organiser is taken away from a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader removed from' drops the M from MARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means chief, as in arch-enemy.

clue.text: Scope for a doctor, it follows

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: Room for a GP, so it follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambit is range or extent, the bounds of something.

clue.text: A number in the surgery?

parts.note: number read as something that numbs, a drug given to dull pain

explanation.surface: A count taken at the doctor's.
explanation.definitionFit: An analgesic numbs pain, so it is literally a number, something that makes numb.

clue.text: Writers following his authority

definitions.meaning: placed after his, it forms a slang title for a big shot

explanation.surface: Authors obeying their chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His nibs' is mocking slang for a self-important person in charge, so the word follows 'his' to mean authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen points are what do the writing, and 'his nibs' is a jokey name for a boss.

clue.text: Exploits customs

explanation.surface: Takes advantage of traditions.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to employ it, and customs are habitual practices.

clue.text: Supervise for a small charge

parts.note: the small charge is a little child in one's care, not a modest fee

explanation.surface: Oversee something for a low fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Minding an infant while the parents are out is looking after a little ward.

clue.text: Turn out in body to find robber

indicators.note: in places the word for turn out inside the word for body

parts.note: a band is a body of people
to rig out is to dress or turn out

explanation.surface: Searching a corpse turns up a thief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RIG inside BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit, an outlaw who robs travellers.

clue.text: Rate revision certain to indicate value

indicators.note: revision reworks the word rate into another arrangement

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: Revised figures are sure to show what something is worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' rearranges RATE into TREA.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure something is to prize or esteem it highly.

clue.text: Remove obstacle in river

indicators.note: in places the obstacle inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales and England
let means hindrance, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: Clear a blockage from a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts LET inside DEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete is to strike out or erase.
